_source_note: MIXED PROVENANCE, DISCLOSED PER-ENTRY. Each entry has a 'provenance' field: 'real' (a genuine, published, verifiable CVE - source_url included, check it yourself) or 'simulated' (fabricated for this prototype to cover a component category with no convenient real public CVE, ID suffixed '-SIM' so it's never mistaken for a resolvable record). Schema mirrors the real NVD structure (https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities) and CVSS v3.1 (https://www.first.org/cvss/v3.1/specification-document). See /REFERENCES.md section 1-2.

entries.description: Nicknamed 'Pantsdown'. ASPEED AST2400/AST2500 BMC hardware and firmware implement AHB bridges allowing arbitrary read/write access to the BMC's physical address space from the host, enabling unauthenticated compromise. Affected numerous OEMs including Supermicro, Gigabyte, IBM, HPE.

Authentication bypass via HTTP header spoofing in AMI MegaRAC BMC's Redfish host interface. Part of the 'BMC&C' vulnerability set disclosed by Eclypsium; affects devices from AMD, Asus, Dell EMC, Gigabyte, HPE, Lenovo, Nvidia, and others using MegaRAC SP-X.
Code injection via AMI MegaRAC's Dynamic Redfish Extension interface, allowing arbitrary code execution as root on the BMC chip. Chains with CVE-2023-34329 for full remote takeover.
